Christmas draws its primary meaning from the biblical announcement of the coming of the Messiah, “The Prince of Peace and of eternal justice” Is.: 9:5-6
👉Peace
“Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth..Luc 2:14
#Christmas #JesusIsKing #tojesusthroughmary
Spiritual origins of Peace and the Christmas Truce
- In the Gospel according to Saint Luke (2:14), the angels proclaim: “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to those whom He loves.”  
- Christmas finds its first meaning in the biblical announcement of the Messiah, called by the prophet Isaiah “Prince of Peace and of eternal justice” (Is 9:5–6). 
- From the beginning, the feast of Christmas has been associated with a universal message of peace and reconciliation.  

2. Institutional origins  
- In the Middle Ages, the Church established the Peace of God and the Truce of God (Treuga Dei) to limit feudal violence.  
- From the 11th century, councils (such as Toulouges in 1027) forbade private battles during sacred periods: Advent and Christmas, Lent and Easter. 
- This measure protected civilians and imposed temporary peace, under penalty of excommunication.  
- The Church did not abolish war but sought to moralize it: the first organized attempt at pacification in medieval Europe.  

3. The Christmas Truce in history
- The Christmas Truce became a powerful symbol, notably during World War I (1914), when German and British soldiers spontaneously ceased fire to sing carols, exchange gifts, and fraternize.  
- This episode illustrates the strength of the Christmas message: even in the heart of conflict, it can inspire a pause and a gesture of humanity.  

4. The institutional message today  
- Each year, the Pope delivers the *Urbi et Orbi* blessing (“to the city and to the world”), calling for universal peace. 
 
- Typical excerpt: 
“May peoples wounded by war find the strength to build a common future… May light triumph over darkness, and may love be stronger than hatred.”  
- This message perpetuates the idea that Christmas is a time of truce and hope for all humanity.  

5. Contemporary and cultural adaptations 
Christmas, though of Christian origin, has taken root in local and multicultural traditions, becoming a moment of family and social peace throughout the world.  

a) - Middle East
- In Syria, the "Christmas camel" brings gifts to children.

- In Iraq, bonfires symbolize the victory of good over evil.

- In the United Arab Emirates, Christmas is celebrated lavishly, promoting tolerance and social harmony.

b) - India
- Christmas is called Bada Din ("the great day").

- Hindi carols and local masses emphasize peace and redemption.

- In tribal communities, indigenous dances and songs strengthen interethnic peace.

c) - Philippines and Southeast Asia
- In the Philippines, Christmas lasts for several months, with the Misa de Gallo and star-shaped "parol" lanterns.

- The government sometimes proclaims military truces to allow families to reunite.

- In Indonesia and Vietnam, Christmas becomes a time of interreligious tolerance.

d) - Oceania
- In Australia, Christmas is celebrated in the middle of summer: barbecues on the beach and carols by candlelight.

- In New Zealand, the Maori blend the haka and Christian hymns for harmony.

- In Fiji, churches decorated with local trees celebrate community peace.

e) - Northern Europe
- In Finland, the Christmas Peace Declaration has been proclaimed every December 24th in Turku since the 13th century.

- In the Scandinavian countries, Christmas is a time of light and inner peace.

f) - Latin America
- Nochebuena (December 24th) is the key moment: a festive meal and midnight mass.

- In Mexico, Posadas recreate the journey of Mary and Joseph, promoting solidarity.

g) - East Asia
- In China, "peace apples" (pingguo) are given as a symbol of goodwill. - In Japan, Christmas is romantic and festive, centered on social harmony.

h) - Anglo-Saxon World
- In the United States and the United Kingdom, Christmas is a time for family reconciliation.
- The 1914 truce is often cited as a symbol of humanity.
- The "Peace on Earth" carols evoke the universal ideal of peace.

i) - Africa
- In East Africa, Christmas is a time for karamu (feasting) to promote family peace.

- In Ethiopia, Nigeria, and South Africa, Christmas is a communal celebration, with dances and prayers for peace.

Throughout the world, Christmas invites us to a universal pause: reconciliation, generosity, and the hope for peace.
Whether religious, cultural, or secular traditions, the message remains the same: Christmas is a time when peace becomes possible, even in the midst of conflict.

data.text:
Plunder of PhilHealth: A Betrayal of Universal Health Care

Authored by Dr. Tony Leachon

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, together with former PhilHealth president Emmanuel Ledesma, now faces plunder charges before the Ombudsman. 

The complaint filed by the Save the Philippines Coalition exposes the unconstitutional diversion of ₱60 billion in PhilHealth funds—resources meant for healthcare services—into the National Treasury.

This was not an accident. It was a premeditated act, engineered through a flawed rider provision in the GAA that siphoned PhilHealth’s earmarked resources into unprogrammed appropriations and flood control projects. 

The result: millions of poor and unemployed Filipinos stripped of health coverage, in direct violation of the Universal Health Care Act and the Sin Tax Law.

Recto cannot feign ignorance. His record reveals a consistent pattern:

• He voted against the Sin Tax in 2012, undermining health reforms.

• He authored regressive taxation measures like VAT, burdening ordinary Filipinos.

• He misled the public with claims of a “record-breaking ₱113 billion subsidy” for PhilHealth, when in truth, ₱60 billion was merely restored by Supreme Court order.

This is technical malversation and plunder. Good faith cannot excuse deliberate defunding. 

The law is clear: PhilHealth funds belong to its members and cannot be diverted without legal basis.

Universal Health Care is not a slogan—it is a covenant. To defund PhilHealth is to betray justice, dignity, and the right to health.

We demand:

• Accountability from those who orchestrated this betrayal.
• Transparency in allocations.
• Judicial enforcement to protect the UHC Act.

Ralph Recto must face the consequences of his actions. 

The fight for PhilHealth funding is the fight for the soul of our healthcare system. Anything less is a betrayal of the nation.

#RelentlessForChange
#Ombudsman #PhilHealth #UHC #Accountability
